title: BC 29 lets a single index span base table and table extension fields
summary: Business Central 29 allows table extension keys to span both base table and extension fields in a single index, eliminating a long-standing constraint. This enables simpler indexing solutions for filtered lists, reporting extractions, and performance problems that previously required architectural workarounds.
key_points: Version 29 removes the restriction that keys must contain either all base table fields or all extension fields, but not both
The change is enabled by storing all AL table fields in the same physical database table instead of separate companion tables
Cross-boundary keys solve real performance problems like filtering on base table fields while sorting on extension fields
Developers must still consider the 40-key-per-table limit and write performance costs when adding new indexes
The capability is in public preview for online sandboxes only; on-premises guidance will follow general availability in October 2026

quotes.text: Every index costs writes. An index that makes one list fast makes every insert and modify on that table slower.
quotes.why_it_matters: Critical caution for developers considering new cross-boundary indexes to avoid unforeseen performance degradation
